newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Camet says gov't has cut poverty since 1991.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Camet says gov't has cut poverty since 1991.

text.p: Peru's Economy Minister Jorge Camet said Wednesday the government's economic policies have slashed poverty since 1991, including a sharp drop in the number of people living in extreme poverty.

"We can say that Peru today, despite its enormous needs, can show the world a notable reduction in the levels of poverty," Camet was quoted as saying at the Inter-American Development Bank's (IADB) annual meeting in Barcelona, Spain.

"Between 1991 and 1994, poverty levels have been reduced by 15 percent and extreme poverty, which affected 25 percent of the population, is today at 19 percent," he was quoted as saying in a statement from Peru's Council of Ministers.
According to the statement, Camet acknowledged that the economic stabilization and free-market reforms implemented by President Alberto Fujimori after taking office in 1990, were "particularly hard."

But he added that "today one cannot doubt the enormous benefit produced by the reforms, not only generating growth and stability in Peru, but setting the foundation for long-term sustained development."
Camet also said Peru this year will seek to attain six percent economic growth, compared with 2.8 percent in 1996, and an inflation rate akin to those of industrialized nations.
In 1996, Peru's fiscal surplus reached 1.1 percent of gross domestic product compared with deficits of 10 percent in the 1980s, he was quoted as saying.

The minister also said fiscal austerity and a tight monetary policy resulted in a stable economy and a reduction in inflation from 7,000 percent in 1990 to an annualized rate of 9.4 percent last month.
He added that Peru's foreign reserves rose from a negative figure in 1990 to $9 billion early this year, or roughly 13 months of exports.
According to the statement, Camet also said investment rose from an equivalent of 15 percent of GDP in 1990 to 24 percent in 1996.
